payload.answer: Architectural hygiene immediately before the codebase grows. Runbooks 16-21 add an operator, a shared-library extraction, two new products and several new modules, and every one of them is a chance to land outside the floors. Closing the gap after that expansion is strictly more work than closing it now. There is also a live example of why uncovered code hides defects: `vibey cost` reads its caps from config['budget']['max_dollars_per_cycle'], a key nothing writes, so it silently displays hardcoded $40/$250 defaults instead of the project's real configured cap. Fixing that is OUT OF SCOPE here -- it is named only as evidence that unexercised code drifts.
